title: Sum of Two Numbers
statement: Read two integers A and B and print their sum.
input_format: One line with two integers A and B.
output_format: A single integer: A + B.
constraints_text: -10^9 <= A, B <= 10^9 (the sum may not fit in a 32-bit integer).

title: Even or Odd
statement: Read an integer N and tell whether it is even or odd. Remember that negative numbers can be even or odd too.
input_format: One line with an integer N.
output_format: Print Even or Odd.

title: Largest of Three
statement: Read three integers and print the largest one.
input_format: One line with three integers A, B and C.
output_format: A single integer: the largest of the three.

title: Sum of 1 to N
statement: Read N and print the sum 1 + 2 + ... + N.
input_format: One line with an integer N.
output_format: A single integer: the sum.

title: Multiplication Table
statement: Read N and print its multiplication table from 1 to 10. Each line must look exactly like `N x i = product`.
input_format: One line with an integer N.
output_format: Ten lines, for i = 1 to 10: `N x i = product`.

title: Factorial
statement: Read N and print N! (N factorial). By definition 0! = 1.
input_format: One line with an integer N.
output_format: A single integer: N!
constraints_text: 0 <= N <= 20 (20! fits in a signed 64-bit integer).

title: Digit Sum
statement: Read a non-negative integer N and print the sum of its decimal digits.
input_format: One line with an integer N.
output_format: A single integer: the digit sum.

title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
statement: Read a temperature in whole degrees Celsius and convert it to Fahrenheit using F = C * 9 / 5 + 32. Print the result with exactly 2 digits after the decimal point.
input_format: One line with an integer C.
output_format: The temperature in Fahrenheit with exactly two decimals.

title: Leap Year
statement: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100 that are not divisible by 400. Read a year and print `Leap Year` or `Not a Leap Year`.
input_format: One line with an integer Y.
output_format: Print Leap Year or Not a Leap Year.

title: FizzBuzz
statement: For every number from 1 to N print one line: `FizzBuzz` if it is divisible by both 3 and 5, `Fizz` if divisible by 3 only, `Buzz` if divisible by 5 only, otherwise the number itself.
input_format: One line with an integer N.
output_format: N lines as described.

output_format: One integer: the second largest distinct value, or -1.

input_format: One line: words made of letters, separated by single spaces.
output_format: The words in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

title: Valid Palindrome
statement: Read a line of text. Ignoring case and every character that is not a letter or a digit, decide whether the text reads the same forwards and backwards. Print YES or NO. A line with no letters or digits counts as a palindrome.
input_format: One line of printable ASCII characters.
output_format: YES or NO.

title: Binary Search Queries
statement: You are given a sorted array of distinct integers and several queries. For each query print the 0-based index of the value in the array, or -1 if it is not present.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N integers in strictly increasing order. Line 3: Q. Line 4: Q integers (the queries).
output_format: Q lines, one answer per query, in order.
constraints_text: 1 <= N, Q <= 10^5, values fit in 32-bit signed integers.

title: Sort the Array
statement: Sort the given integers in non-decreasing order and print them on one line separated by spaces.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N integers.
output_format: The sorted integers separated by spaces.

title: Most Frequent Character
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters print the letter that occurs most often followed by how many times it occurs. If several letters tie, print the alphabetically smallest one.
input_format: One line: a string of lowercase letters.
output_format: The letter, a space, and its count.

title: Rotate Array Right
statement: Rotate the array to the right by K positions (each step moves the last element to the front) and print the result.
input_format: Line 1: N and K. Line 2: N integers.
output_format: The rotated array separated by spaces.

title: Two Sum Indices
statement: Given an array of distinct integers and a target T, there is exactly one pair of positions i < j with a[i] + a[j] = T. Print i and j (0-based).
input_format: Line 1: N and T. Line 2: N distinct integers.
output_format: Two integers i and j with i < j.
constraints_text: 2 <= N <= 10^4, values fit in 32-bit signed integers. Exactly one valid pair exists.

title: Anagram Check
statement: Two words are anagrams if one can be rearranged into the other using every letter exactly once. Decide whether the two given words are anagrams.
input_format: Two lines, each a word of lowercase letters.
output_format: YES or NO.

title: Missing Number
statement: An array contains N-1 distinct integers taken from 1..N in random order. Exactly one number from 1..N is missing. Find it.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: the N-1 integers.
output_format: The missing integer.

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
statement: Merge two arrays that are each sorted in non-decreasing order into one sorted array.
input_format: Line 1: N and M. Line 2: N integers. Line 3: M integers.
output_format: The merged array separated by spaces.

title: Remove Duplicates Keeping Order
statement: Print the array with every repeated value removed, keeping only the first occurrence of each value and preserving the original order.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N integers.
output_format: The remaining values separated by spaces.

title: GCD and LCM
statement: Read two positive integers and print their greatest common divisor and least common multiple.
input_format: One line with integers A and B.
output_format: Two integers: GCD and LCM separated by a space.
constraints_text: 1 <= A, B <= 10^9 (the LCM can be as large as 10^18).

title: Count Primes
statement: Count how many prime numbers are less than or equal to N.
input_format: One line with an integer N.
output_format: One integer: the number of primes <= N.

title: Caesar Cipher
statement: Shift every letter of the text forward in the alphabet by K positions, wrapping from z back to a. Upper-case letters stay upper-case, lower-case stay lower-case and all other characters are unchanged.
input_format: Line 1: K. Line 2: the text.
output_format: The encrypted text.

title: Matrix Diagonals
statement: Given an N x N matrix print the sum of the main diagonal (top-left to bottom-right) and the sum of the anti-diagonal (top-right to bottom-left).
input_format: Line 1: N. Then N lines with N integers each.
output_format: Two integers: main diagonal sum and anti-diagonal sum.

title: Balanced Brackets
statement: A string made only of the characters ( ) [ ] { } is balanced if every opening bracket is closed by the matching bracket in the correct order. Decide whether the string is balanced.
input_format: One line with the string.
output_format: YES or NO.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
statement: Find the largest possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N integers.
output_format: One integer: the maximum subarray sum.

title: Sort by Frequency
statement: Sort the array so that values appearing more often come first. Values with equal frequency are ordered from smaller to larger. Print the sorted array (every occurrence is kept).
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N integers.
output_format: The reordered array separated by spaces.

title: Run-Length Encoding
statement: Compress a string by replacing every run of the same letter with the letter followed by the length of the run. For example aaabbc becomes a3b2c1.
input_format: One line: a string of lowercase letters.
output_format: The encoded string.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of the array (elements need not be adjacent).
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N integers.
output_format: One integer: the length of the LIS.
constraints_text: 1 <= N <= 10^5, -10^9 <= a[i] <= 10^9. An O(N^2) solution is too slow.

title: 0/1 Knapsack
statement: There are N items, each with a weight and a value. Choose a subset of items (each at most once) whose total weight does not exceed W so that the total value is as large as possible.
input_format: Line 1: N and W. Then N lines: weight and value of each item.
output_format: One integer: the maximum total value.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
statement: Given two strings, find the length of their longest common subsequence (characters keep their relative order but need not be adjacent).
input_format: Two lines, each a string of lowercase letters.
output_format: One integer: the LCS length.

title: Edit Distance
statement: The edit distance between two strings is the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions or replacements needed to turn the first string into the second. Compute it.
input_format: Two lines, each a string of lowercase letters.
output_format: One integer: the edit distance.

title: Minimum Coin Change
statement: You have unlimited coins of N different values. Find the minimum number of coins needed to make exactly the amount T, or print -1 if it is impossible.
input_format: Line 1: N and T. Line 2: the N coin values.
output_format: One integer: the minimum number of coins, or -1.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
statement: Decide whether the array can be split into two groups (every element in exactly one group) with equal sums.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N positive integers.
output_format: YES or NO.

title: Weighted Job Scheduling
statement: There are N jobs, each with a start time, an end time and a profit. You can work on one job at a time; a job may start exactly when another ends. Choose non-overlapping jobs to maximise the total profit.
input_format: Line 1: N. Then N lines: start end profit.
output_format: One integer: the maximum total profit.

title: Number of Islands
statement: A grid contains 1 (land) and 0 (water). An island is a maximal group of land cells connected horizontally or vertically. Count the islands.
input_format: Line 1: R and C. Then R lines of C characters (0 or 1).
output_format: One integer: the number of islands.

title: Shortest Path
statement: A network has N cities (numbered 1..N) and M bidirectional roads with lengths. Find the length of the shortest route from city 1 to city N, or -1 if no route exists.
input_format: Line 1: N and M. Then M lines: u v w (a road of length w between u and v).
output_format: One integer: the shortest distance, or -1.

title: Minimum Spanning Tree
statement: Cables must connect N offices. Given the possible cables with their costs, find the minimum total cost so that every office is connected to every other one (directly or indirectly), or print -1 if that is impossible.
input_format: Line 1: N and M. Then M lines: u v w (a cable between u and v costing w).
output_format: One integer: the minimum total cost, or -1.

title: Smallest Topological Order
statement: There are N tasks numbered 1..N and M rules `u v` meaning task u must be done before task v. Print an order that satisfies every rule; if several orders exist print the lexicographically smallest one (compare the sequences number by number). If the rules contradict each other print IMPOSSIBLE.
input_format: Line 1: N and M. Then M lines: u v.
output_format: N task numbers separated by spaces, or IMPOSSIBLE.

title: Grid Paths with Obstacles
statement: A robot starts at the top-left cell of a grid and wants to reach the bottom-right cell, moving only right or down. Cells marked # are blocked. Count the number of different paths modulo 1 000 000 007.
input_format: Line 1: R and C. Then R lines of C characters: . (free) or # (blocked).
output_format: One integer: the number of paths modulo 1000000007.

title: Count Inversions
statement: An inversion is a pair of positions i < j with a[i] > a[j]. Count the inversions in the array.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N integers.
output_format: One integer: the number of inversions (can exceed 32 bits).
constraints_text: 1 <= N <= 10^5, -10^9 <= a[i] <= 10^9. An O(N^2) solution is too slow.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
statement: A histogram has N bars of width 1 with the given heights. Find the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside the histogram.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N heights.
output_format: One integer: the largest area.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: For every window of K consecutive elements of the array, find the largest element in the window. Print the maximum of each window from left to right.
input_format: Line 1: N and K. Line 2: N integers.
output_format: N-K+1 integers separated by spaces.

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: Bars of width 1 and the given heights stand side by side. After it rains, water is trapped between the bars. Compute the total amount of water (in unit squares) that stays trapped.
input_format: Line 1: N. Line 2: N heights.
output_format: One integer: the trapped water.

title: Minimum Window Substring
statement: Find the length of the shortest substring of S that contains every character of T (including repeated characters, so if T has two a's the window needs at least two a's). Print -1 if no such substring exists.
input_format: Two lines: the string S and the string T (lowercase letters).
output_format: One integer: the length of the shortest window, or -1.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
statement: Find the length of the longest substring of the given string that is a palindrome.
input_format: One line: a string of lowercase letters.
output_format: One integer: the length of the longest palindromic substring.

title: Word Break
statement: Given a string S and a dictionary of words, decide whether S can be written as a concatenation of dictionary words. Each word may be used any number of times.
input_format: Line 1: S. Line 2: K. Then K lines, one dictionary word each.
output_format: YES or NO.

title: N-Queens Count
statement: Count the ways to place N queens on an N x N chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no shared row, column or diagonal).
input_format: One line with an integer N.
output_format: One integer: the number of valid placements.
